styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Palace, museums and the grand boulevards.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Old town lanes, churches and the Parliament.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Markets, taverns and long Romanian dinners.

stays.why: The old town: bars, cafés and sights on your doorstep. Noisy at weekends, so ask for a back room.
Next to the Palace of Parliament and the big boulevards. Quieter at night, good metro links.
Central and calm, near the museums and parks. Easy metro and airport bus connections.
Cheapest beds and the main train station. Handy for day trips, but a 25–30 minute walk to the old town.

food: Try the classics: sarmale (stuffed cabbage rolls), mici (grilled sausages) and ciorbă (sour soup).
Look for a 'bistro' or 'cramă' lunch menu; a two-course set lunch is often good value.
Obor market is the place for cheese, produce and cheap local snacks; go in the morning.
Vegetarian and vegan spots are growing fast in the centre; check menus before you go.
Prices vary widely. Check the bill and confirm service charges in touristy old-town places.
more_time: Swap a city day for a train to Brașov or Sinaia; check timetables and buy tickets at Gara de Nord.
Add a half-day at the open-air Village Museum (Muzeul Satului) in Herăstrău park.
Slow down in Cișmigiu or Herăstrău park with a coffee and a walk instead of another museum.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the old town, the Palace of Parliament and a museum or two; add a night for a day trip to the mountains.

month_notes: January: cold, highs near 4°C and lows around -4°C. Pack a warm coat and boots.
February: still cold, highs around 8°C. Fewer tourists and lower prices.
March: milder at about 12°C but expect rain on roughly 9 days.
April: pleasant at 18°C; showers on about 10 days, so carry a light rain jacket.
May: warm and green, highs near 22°C. A great month for parks and walking.
June: hot at 27°C with the most rain days (about 12). Plan indoor breaks.
July: hot, around 30°C. Sightsee early morning and late afternoon.
August: hot like July but drier, with about 6 rain days. Busy holiday season.
September: warm and drier, highs near 25°C. One of the best months to visit.
October: cooler at 18°C with about 6 rain days. Good for museums and cafés.
November: chilly at 11°C and wetter. Bring layers and an umbrella.
December: cold, highs near 7°C. Christmas markets and short daylight; pack warm clothes.

climate_guide.summary: Continental climate: hot summers, cold winters, and rain spread through the year.

items.title: Best time: May, June and September
items.text: Warm days around 22–27°C and long evenings. Ideal for walking the old town and parks.

items.title: Summer can be hot
items.text: July and August reach about 30°C. Sightsee in the morning and evening; rest indoors at midday.

items.title: Winters are cold
items.text: January highs near 4°C and lows around -4°C. Bring a proper coat, hat and warm shoes.

items.title: Rain all year
items.text: Expect roughly 5–12 rain days each month. June is wettest; September is driest. A small umbrella helps.

items.title: Spring and autumn are mild
items.text: April, May and October are comfortable for walking, with highs of 18–22°C.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers, a waterproof jacket and comfortable shoes for cobblestones; a warm coat for December to February.

transit.best: Metro for longer hops, walking in the centre, and Bolt or Uber at night.

modes.text: Four lines, frequent and cheap. Use a contactless card or an Activ card.
Trams and buses are extensive but crowded. Validate your card on boarding.
Use kiosks at the airport for taxis. Uber and Bolt work well in the city.
Traffic is heavy at rush hour and parking is scarce in the centre. Skip it for city days.
The centre is walkable. Bikes are available but bike lanes are limited.
Gara de Nord is the main station for day trips; check timetables on the day.
